HOOK-F01.title: Returning to an already delivered mode suppresses the current persona
HOOK-F01.evidence_level: focused isolated runtime probe + implementation read
HOOK-F01.description: Delivery is keyed by session, mode and compaction generation. In one session/generation, arbiter -> dangerous -> arbiter leaves the original arbiter tuple marked, so the final arbiter effective mode emits no arbiter persona after dangerous was injected.
HOOK-F01.observed: Actual shared mode writes/audits and actual persona files: initial arbiter output10990 characters; dangerous7908; return to arbiter0. This does not disable deterministic tool/Git guards.
HOOK-F01.recommendation: Bind delivery to current successful mode transition epoch or last delivered mode/generation, with monotonic session identity; preserve repeated-event idempotency and independent safety injection.

HOOK-F02.title: Mode flip failure reports no change after raw state has already changed
HOOK-F02.evidence_level: isolated injected append failure + implementation read
HOOK-F02.description: flip writes raw mode before audit settlement. An audit append failure returns FLIP_FAILED; prompt text calls it a marker write error and says the session remains in its current mode. The raw mode can already be ops while effective mode falls back to arbiter because it is not ledger-backed.
HOOK-F02.observed: With _append_override_line forced false: result failed, raw_mode ops, effective_mode arbiter, user_message says marker write error and remains in current mode. Owed audit recovery is implemented; failure is not evidence of total rollback.
HOOK-F02.recommendation: Return typed outcome carrying requested/raw/effective modes, marker commit and audit debt/retry state. Report partial completion honestly; preserve existing recovery and gate fail direction.

HOOK-F03.title: Pi doctor rejects the actual scoped package identity
HOOK-F03.evidence_level: actual checkout payload checked through check_payload
HOOK-F03.description: doctor.check_payload requires package.name == ca-pi; current plugins/ca-pi/package.json and PiHost identify @arbiterforge/ca-pi. It produces a reinstall failure for this otherwise present payload.
HOOK-F03.observed: check_payload(PiHost) on this checkout reports payload version0.27.5 OK, invalid ca-pi discovery contract FAIL, and bridge/support scripts OK.
HOOK-F03.recommendation: Use the actual canonical host/package identity shared with manifest generation and host resolver; retain exact extension/skill discovery validation.

HOOK-F04.title: Qualified npm workspace binding can exceed native completion consumer limit
HOOK-F04.classification: confirmed producer reachability; cross-layer consumer mismatch validated by native agent
HOOK-F04.evidence_level: actual Python producer probe; Go consumer static read by native_states
HOOK-F04.description: The Python producer permits up to32 workspace manifests plus base launch files. Native observation schema permits37, qualified runner permits32 workspace manifests, but completionWorkspacesOnce rejects more than32 launch_files. A qualified operation can reach publication with a producer-valid binding the consumer refuses.
HOOK-F04.observed: Using real npm resolution and temp Git project, without running test commands:30 workspaces ->32 launch files;31->33;32->34 on POSIX. Windows additional launch roles imply up to37 from source, not runtime-probed here.
cross_agent_sources: native_states: observation/contract.go commandBindingSchema; evidence/runner_contract.go validateQualifiedBinding; evidence/completion_workspace.go completionWorkspacesOnce; use native ledger for exact paths/ranges
HOOK-F04.recommendation: Define one versioned launch-binding bound/role contract, derive validators and boundary fixtures across Python/Go. Match accepted producer and completion sets without weakening file fingerprints.

HOOK-F05.title: Spinner uninstall restores backup over a user change made after install
HOOK-F05.evidence_level: isolated settings transformation probe + implementation read
HOOK-F05.description: statusLine uninstall checks exact ownership before restoring. _uninstall_spinner_verbs restores whenever its backup key exists, even if current spinnerVerbs was changed by the user after installation.
HOOK-F05.observed: Current verbs user changed after install plus prior backup becomes prior, losing the current choice.
HOOK-F05.recommendation: Record exact installed spinner ownership value and restore backup only if current still equals it; otherwise preserve current custom state and remove obsolete backup metadata.

HOOK-B01.title: Debug validator rejection is stateless and does not prove authorization denial
HOOK-B01.description: _debughandofflib imports no filesystem/process/network facility and maintains no rejection ledger. Each CLI invocation independently validates shape/references/internal semantics. Exit2 includes correctable input failures; exit3 operational failures. Root audit should compare one-shot resubmission prose against this distinction.
HOOK-B01.recommendation: Separate invalid transport/shape/reference input, unsupported causal evidence and denied authorization in the contract. Allow bounded correction of shape for the same authorized scope without silently widening authority; preserve substantive causal/regression requirements.

HOOK-B02.title: Per-turn prompt owns persona delivery; SessionStart owns startup side effects
HOOK-B02.description: prompt-submit composes/dedups safety and mode persona, and PreCompact changes delivery generation. SessionStart does mode housekeeping/statusline repair before activation, installs Git backstop when active, then initialized briefing and detached refresh. Documentation claiming persona injection is owned solely by SessionStart is stale.
HOOK-B02.recommendation: Generate event-to-owner documentation from the implemented hook contract and retain a passive explicit-root inspection route for unfamiliar repos.

HOOK-B03.title: Security review marker binds the complete staged candidate, not just sensitive lines
HOOK-B03.description: The marker includes worktree identity, whole staged diff binding and sensitive diagnostics. Consumer requires all matching. Unrelated staged edits invalidate this proof. Producing the marker does not independently verify semantic reviewer PASS; the higher-level workflow owns that obligation.
HOOK-B03.recommendation: Document the actual candidate boundary and generate recovery text from it; preserve complete-diff invalidation until an intentionally reviewed narrower evidence model exists.

HOOK-B04.title: No startup or knowledge backstop scans stranded terminal harvest residue
HOOK-B04.classification: confirmed absence within inspected entrypoint/helper scope
HOOK-B04.evidence_level: complete executable-source read of relevant runtime family
HOOK-B04.description: SessionStart daily standup checks Git/task/provenance/update state, and knowledge.py handles selected native knowledge edits/conversion/promotion/staleness. Neither implements a durable scan for an unharvested terminal workflow obligation. Root prose audit owns whether such an obligation is promised.
HOOK-B04.recommendation: If harvest is mandatory, persist an explicit retryable per-workflow obligation and expose it in status/recovery; do not infer obligations from unrelated board prose or rerun successful external effects.

HOOK-B05.title: Native client accepts optional context qualification field
HOOK-B05.description: ArtifactClient._open_binary accepts either five release-manifest fields or those plus context_qualification. The farm consumer exact-five check found by host agent has a narrower acceptance set. Python method does not itself validate optional field value.
HOOK-B05.recommendation: Use one versioned manifest schema for producers and consumers, retaining explicit platform/native-tested/digest checks. Host/native ledgers own candidate qualification effects.

W-F01.title: Conflict command prescribes a broader stop than the assistive engine contract
W-F01.detail: The conflict command says all work stops when governing rules conflict. Current sprint/context guidance and ADR0043 describe refusal scoped to dependent work. These cannot both be a universal rule. Source does not implement a single dependency-aware conflict controller.
W-F01.recommendation: Choose and document the stop scope explicitly. Recommend stop affected authority/data dependencies, preserve independent read-only work, and keep genuine global host/user stops global. This is a policy decision, not a silent prose cleanup.

W-F02.title: Debug handoff treats a correctable packet error as a terminal one-shot boundary
W-F02.detail: The workflow forbids repairing and resubmitting any rejected packet. The validator is stateless and distinguishes malformed/invalid packets from internal I/O errors; it records no consumed one-shot capability. The prose therefore imposes an extra recovery policy beyond implementation.
W-F02.recommendation: Separate invalid input, denied authority, stale binding and internal failure. Permit an explicitly corrected new input attempt where authority remains valid; retain the refusal for an unchanged denied request. Requires approved workflow-policy change.

W-F03.title: Maintenance severity and reviewer disposition conflict
W-F03.detail: The dependency reviewer can report HIGH maintenance risk while saying not to block on maintenance alone. The included reviewer contract says every HIGH is blocking and additions never replace that rule. This makes a correct verdict ambiguous for the reviewing agent and user.
W-F03.recommendation: Represent severity and disposition separately; document the explicit maintenance-only disposition exception or revise its severity. Generate the common verdict contract from the selected policy.

W-F04.title: Terminal finding harvest has no implemented recovery for interruption before the terminal step
W-F04.detail: Several workflows harvest qualifying findings at completion. The knowledge helper and session/standup paths do not implement a durable pending-harvest backstop. An interrupted run can therefore leave eligible findings only in conversation; the source does not prove every such finding is lost.
W-F04.recommendation: Keep harvest opportunistic. If durable recovery is desired, record bounded pending candidates at discovery and settle/deduplicate on completion/resume. Register any new output with all native readers; do not introduce a new universal completion gate.

W-F05.title: SessionStart persona documentation contradicts the prompt-submit owner
W-F05.detail: Init/porting language attributes persona injection to SessionStart. The implemented SessionStart path and ADR0030 place full composed persona delivery in UserPromptSubmit; a mode revisitation bug is documented separately in the hooks findings.
W-F05.recommendation: Make prompt-submit the documented delivery owner and distinguish session setup, selected mode, committed mode and delivered persona.

W-F06.title: Sensitive-lines-only override wording understates the implemented candidate binding
W-F06.detail: The override surface describes an invalidation scope around sensitive lines. The security pass and binding helper retain full candidate/worktree/sensitive digests and hash the complete staged UTF8 diff. A user cannot reliably predict grant reuse from the narrower wording.
W-F06.recommendation: Document the exact binding tuple and invalidation event. Preserve current security semantics while deriving override help from the same binding definition.

W-F07.title: Watch confuses absence of agent polling with absence of CLI polling
W-F07.detail: The watch command describes gh pr checks --watch as server-side blocking with no polling interval. The official gh command documents --interval with default10seconds. Waiting in one detached CLI invocation avoids model-driven polling, but the underlying CLI still refreshes periodically.
W-F07.recommendation: Say one detached gh watch process with no repeated agent calls; preserve its timeout/cancel behavior. Correct the no-polling claim.

W-F08.title: Command catalog and reviewer index drift from their owner bodies
W-F08.detail: COMMANDS.md calls Tribunal eleven-lens while the current owner/reference set contains thirteen. Its release signature uses --dry-run and SemVer-only language where the current owner uses --dryrun and supports numeric sequence targets. The agent index also presents coverage behavior more strongly than the coverage reviewer body does.
W-F08.recommendation: Generate signatures, lens count and index descriptions from explicit owner metadata; do not change actual command spelling or verdict rules just to match stale summaries.

W-F09.title: Compatibility-removal metadata encodes a different policy than the public owner
W-F09.detail: command-routes.json removalRequires is minor-release-with-changelog-notice. build-surface.py enforces that literal vocabulary. The command compatibility policy describes a major/1.0 floor plus a separate approved removal decision and fresh evidence. The release-state observer does not enforce removalRequires. This is a dormant metadata/policy conflict, not proof of an unauthorized live alias removal.
W-F09.recommendation: Choose the approved retirement rule, give it one owner and generate both policy prose and accepted registry values. Preserve existing aliases until the separately approved removal conditions are met.

GEN-F01.title: Prune nudge threshold describes total context instead of freed context
GEN-F01.description: Configuration table says CODEARBITER_PRUNE_NUDGE_MIN_TOKENS sets minimum model-context size. Current nudge_decision compares estimated tokens from rec.context_bytes_freed to threshold. No runtime behavior change is recommended for this documentation correction.
GEN-F01.recommendation: Describe freed avoidable context accurately and derive this predicate/default from an executable contract instead of maintaining a second semantic description.

GEN-F02.classification: confirmed extractor limitation and overbroad generated claim
GEN-F02.title: Hook reference is a bounded static extraction, not all actual runtime message text
GEN-F02.description: Generated intro says it can never drift from what a hook prints. scanMessage drops variable/helper message suffixes, variable tag resolution is limited to30 lines, and skipped calls are not extracted. Current _bashguardlib security blocks append dynamic recovery strings. Literal-tag pass also omits codeMask test, so quoted/commented examples can be extracted as real calls; this latter false-positive possibility is static, not a demonstrated current site occurrence.
GEN-F02.recommendation: Label static templates/omitted dynamic pieces and display extraction gaps; use a typed gate registry or robust AST extraction for canonical IDs/events/recovery while keeping actual runtime code authoritative.

GEN-B01.classification: static helper edge case, current production reachability not demonstrated
GEN-B01.title: Slug suffix counts do not reserve all output slugs
GEN-B01.description: assignSlugs tracks each base independently. The input sequence foo,foo,foo-2 produces foo,foo-2,foo-2 by direct control-flow inspection. Current installed-source names were not evaluated for such a collision in this supplemental read.
GEN-B01.recommendation: If arbitrary names remain supported, reserve emitted slugs globally and fail or consistently disambiguate collisions. Preserve previously published URL redirects when changing assignment.
